species.name: Crappie
why: Water 64°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 6–22 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 70 ft, so fish stay above it.

species.name: White bass
why: Water 64°F on top, a bit cool for them, so they feed in the warmest water they can find.
Best water today is 8–22 ft deep, mostly on wind-blown banks.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 70 ft, so fish stay above it.
Southeast wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the northwest shore: try the wind-blown banks.

species.name: Largemouth bass
why: Water 64°F on top, much colder than they like, so they move slowly and stay deep.
Best water today is 2–20 ft deep, mostly on channel edges.
The lake is layered: warm water down to about 50 ft, cold below.
Little oxygen below about 70 ft, so fish stay above it.
Southeast wind at 10 mph pushes bait onto the northwest shore: try the wind-blown banks.
